description: Aura Phase-T — Production rollout + hardening. After Phase-CLEANUP1+2 closed the code-health backlog (25 commits 2026-05-17), the codebase is clean enough to invest in operational discipline. This phase wires the operational layer the system has been missing: docker-compose prod overlay, version-baked-from-git, automated backup verification, observability dashboards over the already-existing authz_decisions and tool_attempts tables, and a runbook that lets the operator (Davide) rebuild from cold within 30 minutes after a disaster. Pattern source: memory `project_next_milestone_production_simplify_2026-05-15` 'dopo US-A19: prod completa + semplificazione con pattern 2026'. Order is highest-reliability-leverage first. Each story is a single atomic commit on master.

userStories.title: Add compose.prod.yaml overlay with restart, healthcheck thresholds, no debug ports
userStories.description: Create a docker-compose production overlay that the operator can use via `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.prod.yaml up -d`. The overlay tightens the dev defaults without forking the base file. (a) Add `compose.prod.yaml` to repo root. (b) For the `aura` service: set `restart: unless-stopped`, narrow `ports:` to ONLY `127.0.0.1:8080` (no 18080 dashboard exposure on LAN in prod — operator uses ssh tunnel); add `AURA_HEADLESS=true` env. (c) For supporting sidecars (qdrant, garage, searxng, llama-embed, markitdown): `restart: unless-stopped`, healthcheck intervals tightened (30s → 60s once-warm), no host-port exposure where not required. (d) Add a `--profile prod-only` gate on debug-bin sidecars that don't run in prod. (e) Document the overlay in docs/RUNBOOK.md (US-T06 will expand this). (f) Verify with `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.prod.yaml config` that the merged file is valid (no exec — the config command just validates).
acceptanceCriteria: compose.prod.yaml exists in repo root
aura service has restart: unless-stopped and AURA_HEADLESS=true in the overlay

docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.prod.yaml config validates (exit 0) without changes pushing to actual containers
RUNBOOK.md (or a new docs/deploy-prod.md) gets a 1-paragraph note pointing to the overlay (full runbook ships in US-T06)

userStories.notes: Pure infra story — no Go code changes required. The overlay is additive (does NOT modify compose.yaml). Don't include garage/searxng deletion; those stay in dev.

userStories.title: Bake git SHA + tag into version, surface via --version and /api/health
userStories.description: Aura currently logs `version=3.0 commit=dev date=unknown` because the binary doesn't get build-time injected values. (a) Add internal/release/version.go variables Version, Commit, BuildDate as `var ... = "dev"` defaults. (b) Update the build path (Dockerfile + go build invocations in scripts) to use `-ldflags "-X github.com/aura/aura/internal/release.Commit=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) -X ...Date=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"`. (c) Add a `--version` flag handler in cmd/aura/main.go that prints SHA + date + go runtime version and exits 0 BEFORE any setup. (d) Update /api/health JSON response to include `version`, `commit`, `build_date` fields. (e) The aura:local Docker tag stays — but the build args inject SHA. (f) Update the boot-time slog Info to use real values not 'dev'/'unknown'. (g) Verify locally: build, run `./aura --version`, see SHA.
acceptanceCriteria: internal/release/version.go exists with Version, Commit, BuildDate package vars (string)
Dockerfile build step passes -ldflags injecting Commit + BuildDate
cmd/aura/main.go handles --version flag (prints + exits 0 before setup)
/api/health JSON returns version, commit, build_date keys
Boot-time slog 'aura starting' line uses the injected Commit instead of 'dev'
go build ./... green
go test ./internal/release/... green (add a basic version-vars-defined test)
go test ./... green
Single atomic commit prefix: feat(release): inject git SHA + build date at link time (US-T02)
userStories.notes: ldflags pattern is well-known — example: -ldflags="-X 'pkg.Version=$(VERSION)'". Watch for Windows-vs-Linux path quirks; the GoReleaser config (if it exists in scripts/) probably already does this for releases.

userStories.title: Backup-verify cron: daily SQLite restore-into-tmp + integrity check + alert
userStories.description: Aura has a debug_backup harness (cmd/debug_backup) but no scheduled verification. Without verification, backups silently rot. (a) Add internal/dbrecovery/verify.go with a function VerifyBackup(ctx, backupPath, expectMinRows map[string]int) that: copies the backup into a tmpfile, opens it, runs PRAGMA integrity_check, asserts row counts on `principals`, `actors`, `conversations`, `scheduled_tasks` are >= the expected minimums. (b) Add a scheduled_task entry (via the existing cron.Scheduler) that runs daily at 04:00 local (the existing system clock — re-use cfg.Timezone). (c) On failure: send a Telegram alert via the existing alert path (whatever the cron channel uses to send operator messages). (d) On success: emit slog Info with row counts + integrity_check OK. (e) Add a TEST that creates a known-good DB, calls VerifyBackup, asserts pass; and a known-bad DB (truncated), asserts fail.
acceptanceCriteria: internal/dbrecovery/verify.go exists with VerifyBackup(ctx, backupPath, expectMinRows) function
VerifyBackup runs PRAGMA integrity_check + asserts table row counts
Cron schedule wired to run daily (via existing internal/cron.Scheduler, not a separate goroutine)
Failure path emits a Telegram message via the existing cron alert channel (not a new direct send)
Success path emits slog Info with verification report
internal/dbrecovery/verify_test.go covers happy path + truncated DB failure
go build ./... green
go test ./internal/dbrecovery/... green
go test ./... green
Single atomic commit prefix: feat(dbrecovery): daily backup-verify cron with integrity check (US-T03)
userStories.notes: Re-use existing alert channel; DON'T introduce a new direct-to-Telegram path. The scheduler accepts function callbacks; wire VerifyBackup as one. Backup path comes from cfg.BackupPath (or wherever debug_backup reads from).

userStories.title: Surface authz_decisions in dashboard: denial rate + recent denied actors
userStories.description: The authz_decisions table exists and is written by every Authorize call, but nothing surfaces the data. Operators can't see which capabilities are being denied or why. (a) Add /api/maintenance/authz endpoint handler. Returns JSON: denial_rate_24h (float 0-1), top_denied_capabilities (list of {capability, count} sorted desc, 24h window), recent_denials (last 50, with actor_id + capability + reason + created_at — actor_id may be Telegram username or actor UUID). (b) Wire the handler in internal/api/maintenance.go (or wherever the existing maintenance handlers live). (c) Add a basic table panel in the dashboard React (web/src/...) — a new tab under Maintenance called 'Authz' with the 3 sections. (d) Add a handler test that seeds 10 authz_decisions rows + asserts the JSON shape + counts. (e) The dashboard component is keep-it-simple: 3 stacked sections, no charts, no realtime updates.

userStories.title: Production runbook: cold install, upgrade, restore, secret rotation
userStories.description: Document the operational procedures Davide needs after the binary ships. This is the 'lose your SSD, rebuild in 30 minutes' doc. (a) Create docs/RUNBOOK.md with sections: Cold Install (steps from bare Linux box to running Aura including secret-bootstrap), Upgrade (image rebuild + zero-downtime swap via docker compose up -d), Rollback (the previous tag, the seconds it takes), SQLite Restore Drill (steps for a real backup restore from garage/local), Telegram Token Rotation (the exact bot-talk-to-BotFather sequence + cfg update + restart), Mistral API Key Rotation (env update + restart), llama-embed Rebuild (Wave 2.10 install-bootstrap entry point). (b) Each section is concrete — copy-pasteable commands, not abstract narrative. (c) Cross-reference docs/audit-* artifacts where relevant. (d) Add a 'Common Failure Modes' appendix: container restart loop, SQLite locked, Qdrant collection missing, Mistral 429 — each with diagnosis + fix.
